title: 10 min instant ragi dosa | Finger Millet Dosa | Quickly Ragi Dosa | Breakfast Recipe | Kunal kapur recipe
description: जब झटपट कुछ tasty और healthy हो खाना, तब ये रागी डोसा बनाना! This is my humble take on our breakfast Dosa, which is a better option for your breakfast or snacks craving. It's super healthy, tasty and easy to make. This is one of our favourite weekend breakfast. What's more? Learn how to   #RagiDosa #InstantDosa #QuickDosa #BreakfastRecipe #KunalKapurRecipes #InstantRecipes #KKitchen  #dosarecipe #dosachutneyrecipe #southindianfood   -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------  00:00 Introduction 00:23. Instant Dosa Recipe  02:05 Ginger Chutney Recipe 04:53 Making Dosas with the Batter  06:50 Learn about Ragi or Finger Millets with me (Extra Shots) 07:39 Bloopers  Here is how you can make Instant Ragi Dosa.  (Ragi dosa, Ginger Chutney) Makes 8nos Ingredients:  Ragi flour (finger millet) - 1cup Rice flour - ¼ cup Semolina - ½ cup Curd - ¼ cup  Ginger finely chopped - 2tsp Green chilli finely chopped - 2tsp Cumin - 1tsp Water - 1¼ cup Salt - ¼ tsp  Ginger Chutney (inji thuviyal or állam pachadi) Oil - 2 tbsp Channa dal - 1tbsp Urad dal - 1 tbsp Dry red chilli - 4nos Oil - 2 tbsp Ginger sliced - 1 cup Tamarind (seedless)  - a small piece Salt  Jaggery - 1tsp Water - ¼ cup (approx)   For tempering:  Oil - 1tbsp Mustard seeds - 1tsp Curry leaves - a handful   Method: Heat oil and add channa dal, urad dal and dry chilli. Roast them on low heat till dal turns light brown. Let this cool a bit and then dry grind it coarsely. In the same pan add some oil and then add chopped ginger to it. Cook on low heat for 3-4 mins.  Now add the sautéed ginger to the coarse mixture along with jaggery, salt and a dash of water. Grind to a fine thick paste.  Don't forget to 'Like & Share' for more healthy videos.  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------  Hi, I am Chef Kunal Kapur and this is my space, my channel. asr.full_text: music Everyone loves to eat Dosas, right? Everyone loves it. But a dosa requires bit of hard work, little bit of time. And there is an instant method. And today we will make Instant dosa, In this I will use preparing Ragi Dosa! You will need Ragi Dosa if you have it It is very simple to prepare and simple to prepare There is no need of fermentation It becomes quick Let us prepare Ragi Dosa To this, I will be using Ginger Tuviyel With that I will serve, Inji Toeyal, which is also called as Alam Pachadi, Or Ginger Chutney, There, South Indian style ginger chutney, It has some spicy, some spiciness, Because of good amount of ginger. But first of all, So we have to make batter to make Ragi Dosa, This is Ragi, which is also known as Nachni, Or Madua. And we also know this as Finger Mill madwa, and even finger millet. This is ragi flour. In this, we will add rice flour. In this we will add semolina. These are soft maize flour. They give their crispiness. In this we will add yogurt. to this we will add Curd to this we will add little chopped ginger little green chilies and little cumin seeds along with this we will add salt now we will add water now we will mix it well, this brown color is because of raggi, see this is the batter , it is ready. We will give it a rest of 10 to 15 minutes, then again put a little water in it to correct its consistency, until it is got any rest, we will make this ginger chutney. Pour a little water in the pot, and then mix well. Meanwhile, let's prepare Ginger Chutney. For the Ginger Chutney, firstly take some oil. Then add Urad Dal and Chana Dal Then add dry red chilli powder and sauté this Idea behind this was to add light brown colored lentil You see, ginger is a very healthy ingredient and in south of India, different types of chutneys are made and ginger chutney has different taste a little sharp taste but, with dosa. The dal has roasted, the roast color has properly reached the top. We will take it out. Now we will move to ginger. Add a little bit of oil to the same pan. Now we will add roughly cut ginger. We need to cook the ginger in a slow medium flame too. Here in the oil, we will add 1tbsp of Ginger and let it reduce for 30 minutes. Do not fry it for too long. After 30 mins add another 1tsp of Oil. Now add 1tsp of Ginger and let it fry for another 5-7 mins. After 5 mins add 1tsp of Oil and the next time add a little ginger. Now heat a pan on medium flame and add a little oil in it. its color has changed, we'll close it and we'll remove it out into a bowl We'll allow this to cool down a bit Now in a grinder, we'll add this Now we add some jaggery to it but only a little What happens by adding the jaggery, the sharpness of the Ginger, becomes a bit round off So, the jagness of that ginger gets rounded off. So Gouda is important. Also, we will add tamarind. Add Salt. A little water. And we will now grind it. Mix it easily until the batter absorbs the batter. Now our ginger chutney is ready. now we will fill it with our ginger chutney. there are two ways to fill it. either you can add a tempering of curry leaves and mustard seeds on it or you can serve it as it is... It's up to you. We'll add some oil into this pan Heat some oil put mustard seeds on it Add curry leaves and this will go on the chutney Look at that! Bright red, green! Beautiful! The chutney is ready, Now, let's move towards Dosa batter First of all, we will heat up the Dosa pan. As you can see, It has become quite thick, let's add some water to this. There you go, we it has become very thick. Now, we will add a little water. There you go. It's the runner of the batter I gave you, the batter is ready. So now, let's make Dosa, we will add the batter in the center. And we will spread it evenly, just like that, just like a dosa. Now, we will add a little bit of Oil on the top, then, we will cook it slowly, so that nice colour comes out and makes it crispy, alright let's turn this, nice, we get nice brown colour, now we will transfer it, Dosa is ready, now we will make 3-4 more of it, because we don't want to have a mess, we will need more, This one is almost ready, let's make 3-4 so that it comes to bite size, We will need more, It's like an art now. But, It wasn't so important. Now the two of them are getting along. We're starting to feel together. After 1 hour, take off your flame and place on a plate. Serve on a plate without adding your favorite filling. And our ragi dosa is ready. On extra shots, we get more details about ragi. I was to Utarkhand just a fewam. I had a video where I spoke about Ragi couple of months back at the place in Uttarakhand. Lets watch it. This is a finger millet, the structure is exactly like your fingers and there are a few seeds lying on top. These are called finger millet, sometimes it is called Ragi and also known as Madhua in Uttarakhand it's also fresh it's harvested when all of it has been dried it's then ground into dough and made into Madhui ki Roti which is a little reddish in colour because raageya is slightly reddish and it's very tasty we have removed the tiny little peels even though those aren't dried they are not even dry yet. They are still fresh. So the dough can't be made by then. But it takes time for it to absorb this. It's gluten-free. I've been eating this for a long time out in India. Slowly, the flour has refined and become more durable now. What happened with my face? Bye
